tour.overview:
In 710 the imperial court settled in Nara, Japan's first permanent capital, built on the model of the Chinese capital Chang'an. In the 74 years before it moved on, Buddhism flourished under the emperors' protection, and Emperor Shomu ordered a colossal bronze Buddha to protect the country from epidemics and unrest. Nara's temples, shrines and the primeval forest of Mount Kasuga have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998.

This private day from Kyoto or Osaka shows Nara with a licensed guide and a car. You walk among the free-roaming deer of Nara Park, considered messengers of the gods, stand before the Great Buddha of Todai-ji, follow lantern-lined paths to Kasuga Taisha, see the pagoda of Kofuku-ji and have lunch in Naramachi, a quarter of old wooden merchant houses.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Kyoto or Osaka
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 6 km on park paths

WHAT YOU SEE
• Nara Park and its deer.
• Todai-ji: the Nandaimon gate and the Great Buddha Hall.
• Kasuga Taisha.
• Kofuku-ji and its five-storey pagoda.
• Naramachi.

WHY THIS WORKS
We reach Todai-ji at opening time, before the school groups, and the car saves the long walk between the station and the temples.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, first-time visitors and anyone who loves Buddhist art and history.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have only one day for temples, choose our Kyoto tours; Nara is best as a second or third day.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The deer are wild: they can nip or butt when they see food. Buy shika senbei biscuits only from the official stalls and feed them quickly. Todai-ji is very busy from late morning.

days.name: Nara Park and its deer, Todai-ji's Great Buddha, Kasuga Taisha, Kofuku-ji and Naramachi
days.description:
What to expect: the temples of Japan's first capital and its sacred deer, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel in Kyoto or Osaka at about 7:45 for the drive of about an hour. You enter Nara Park, where some 1,300 sika deer roam freely; according to legend, a god arrived in Nara riding a white deer, and they have been protected as sacred ever since. Many have learned to bow to visitors holding the rice biscuits sold in the park.

You pass through the Nandaimon, the Great South Gate, guarded by two wooden Nio kings more than 8 metres tall carved in 1203, and reach the Daibutsuden, the Great Buddha Hall of Todai-ji. Rebuilt in 1709 at two-thirds of its original size, it was until recently the largest wooden building in the world. Inside sits the Daibutsu, a bronze Vairocana Buddha almost 15 metres tall, first cast in 752 using much of Japan's bronze. Behind it, a pillar has a hole the size of the Buddha's nostril: those who squeeze through are said to be granted enlightenment.

You walk through the forest along paths lined with moss-covered stone lanterns to Kasuga Taisha, the shrine of the Fujiwara family, founded in 768, with its vermilion buildings and some 3,000 lanterns, all lit only twice a year at the lantern festivals in February and August. After lunch in Naramachi, a quarter of narrow wooden machiya townhouses that once belonged to merchants, you see the five-storey pagoda of Kofuku-ji, the second-tallest in Japan, and its national treasure hall. You drive back to Kyoto or Osaka, arriving at about 16:00; on request we stop at Fushimi Inari on the way.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:45 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:45 – Nara Park and its deer.
09:15 – Todai-ji and the Great Buddha.
10:45 – Kasuga Taisha.
12:15 – Lunch in Naramachi.
13:30 – Kofuku-ji.
14:30 – Drive back.
16:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Keep paper and maps out of reach of the deer: they eat paper.
• The Kofuku-ji National Treasure Museum, with the famous six-armed Ashura statue, can be added.
• From Osaka, the drive is about 45 minutes.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha tickets, deer biscuits, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Kofuku-ji museum, drinks with lunch.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do the deer really bow?
faq.answer: Many do, especially when they see deer biscuits. Bow to them and they often bow back. Remember they are wild and can nip if you tease them.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall and Kasuga Taisha's inner precinct. Nara Park is free.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch in Naramachi. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we start from Osaka?
faq.answer: Yes. Nara is about 45 minutes from Osaka and an hour from Kyoto by car.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a favourite with children: the deer, the giant Buddha and the pillar to crawl through. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Paths are wide and mostly flat; Kasuga Taisha has gentle slopes and gravel. The car can drop you near each site.

faq.question: Can we combine Nara and Fushimi Inari?
faq.answer: Yes. Fushimi Inari is on the way back to Kyoto and can be added at the end of the day.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, and a bag that closes: the deer are curious.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn are lovely; in early summer you may see fawns, and in February and mid-August the lantern festivals light Kasuga Taisha.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
